claims.text: A hybrid CE-DFT and AIMD-trained MLP methodology can accurately predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for RHEAs in the 1600–2000 °C regime.
The hybrid methodology overcomes the computational cost of direct AIMD for screening large compositional spaces.
The hybrid methodology avoids the inaccuracies of standard empirical potentials in highly distorted lattices.
Near-equiatomic NbMoTaW can form a BCC solid-solution refractory high-entropy alloy.
HfNbTaTiZr is a disordered BCC solid solution under the proposed initial conditions.
Atomic-size differences among HEA constituents cause severe local lattice distortion.
The relevant RHEAs form short-range-order clusters.
Severe local lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion.
Local lattice distortion and short-range order alter the phonon density of states and thereby influence entropy of fusion and heat capacity.
A cluster-expansion Hamiltonian can map the configurational energy landscape of the BCC RHEA lattice with the accuracy needed for melting-property prediction.
Canonical-ensemble AIMD with a Nose thermostat and femtosecond resolution has been used to model liquid density in multicomponent HEAs at approximately 1600 °C.
An MLP trained on AIMD trajectories spanning the solid-liquid transition can capture anharmonic effects and liquid density.
Standard empirical potentials fail because they cannot represent composition-dependent local distortions and specific electronic interactions in multicomponent RHEAs.
DFT parameterization makes the cluster expansion sufficiently accurate for static configurational energies.
The MLP enables efficient phase-space sampling of anharmonic vibrations and liquid-structure evolution sufficient to determine melting and thermodynamic properties.
The hybrid method will predict RHEA melting temperatures within ±50 K of experiment.
The hybrid method will provide accurate entropy-of-fusion and heat-capacity predictions.
Trial-and-error experimental screening is extremely costly and time-consuming for quinary and higher-order alloy spaces.
The proposed method is valid specifically for BCC systems with at least five principal components and severe lattice distortion.
The method may fail when brittle intermetallic formation, liquid segregation, or evaporation of low-melting elements dominates phase behavior.
